title: Why Does a Week Have 7 Days?
lines: Why does a week have {7 days?~seven days?}
Almost everything on your calendar comes from the sky. | Except the week.
{A day is one spin/~A day is one spin} of the Earth.
A month is roughly one lunar cycle, about {29.5 days.~twenty-nine and a half days.}
A year is one trip around the Sun.
{But nothing up there/~But nothing up there} takes a week. | And twice, {whole countries/~whole countries} tried to abolish it.
One theory: each of the Moon's {4 phases~four phases} lasts a little over {7 days.~seven days.}
But historians trace the seven back to Babylon, where sky-watchers tracked seven moving lights.
The Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
Seven wanderers, | and seven became a sacred number.
The Jewish week, six days of work, then a Sabbath, | made seven a steady rhythm.
Christianity and Islam later carried it across the world.
Meanwhile, Roman astrologers gave {each day/~each day} to one of those lights. | The names survive.
Saturday is Saturn's day. | Sunday, the Sun's. | Monday, the Moon's.
French keeps the rest: | mardi, Mars. Mercredi, Mercury. | Jeudi, Jupiter. Vendredi, Venus.
English swapped in Norse gods: | Tyr, Woden, Thor and Frigg.
Revolutionary France tried a {10-day week~ten-day week} in {1793.~seventeen ninety-three.} | It lasted {12 years.~twelve years.}
{The Soviets tried/~The Soviets tried} {5-~five-} and {6-day weeks.~six-day weeks.} | By {1940,~nineteen forty,} seven was back.
Empires fell. Calendars changed. | The seven-day week outlived them all.
Under the Soviet {5-day week,~five-day week,} did everyone get the same day off? | Yes, one shared day off, | or no, it rotated? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: In {1793,~seventeen ninety-three,} France tried to replace the week with {10 days.~ten days.}
